data.name: Zavix Tower
data.detailed_description:
Zavix Tower is a challenging fantasy roguelike turn-based CRPG set in a never ending tower!

Recruit, level, gear up, and develop a group powerful adventurers as you climb the tower.

  • 7 Playable Hero Classes
  • More than 100 Skills
  • More than 30 Unique Mobs.
  • 10 Unique Bosses
  • Large Talent Trees For Each Class
  • Tons Of Gear (limitless)
  • Endless Tower

Can you defeat the Demons and cleanse Zavix Tower?

data.short_description: Zavix Tower is an old-school, party-based, first-person CRPG with rogue-like elements, an upgrade-able and persistent town, and turn-based combat.

reviews.review:
Zavix Tower is a traditional fantasy dungeon crawler that puts character development, tactical combat, equipment hunting, and long-term party progression ahead of elaborate storytelling or cinematic presentation. Developed by Batholith Entertainment and published by Indie Voyage, it draws heavily from classic first-person computer RPGs while incorporating roguelike ideas and an effectively endless tower to explore. Its premise is intentionally simple: assemble a capable group of adventurers, enter the tower, defeat increasingly dangerous creatures, gather better equipment, and continue improving until the party can survive challenges that previously seemed overwhelming.

Party building provides much of the game's strategic depth. Players can recruit characters from seven different hero classes, allowing groups to be constructed around different combinations of offensive power, defense, support, and utility. More than 100 skills are available across the character-development systems, accompanied by substantial talent trees that provide room for specialization. Progression therefore involves more than simply increasing basic statistics. Deciding how individual heroes should develop and making their abilities complement the rest of the group becomes increasingly important as the difficulty rises.

Combat follows a turn-based structure that emphasizes planning rather than quick reactions. Every encounter provides an opportunity to evaluate which abilities should be used, which enemies deserve immediate attention, and how the party's resources should be managed. The first-person dungeon perspective and grid-oriented exploration reinforce the game's old-school identity. While these mechanics can initially appear straightforward, stronger enemies expose weaknesses in poorly constructed parties and encourage players to reconsider their skills, equipment, and overall team composition.

Equipment is one of the strongest incentives to keep climbing. Zavix Tower is heavily focused on loot, with an enormous number of potential equipment combinations giving players frequent opportunities to discover upgrades. Finding a valuable weapon, piece of armor, or other useful item can noticeably improve a character and occasionally influence the direction of an entire build. Players who enjoy comparing statistics and repeatedly optimizing equipment are likely to get considerably more mileage from the game than those who view inventory management as an inconvenience.

The tower's effectively endless nature is simultaneously one of the game's biggest attractions and one of its main limitations. There is always another challenge to pursue and another opportunity to strengthen the party, making it suitable for players who enjoy repetitive progression loops. However, the environments and encounters eventually become familiar. With more than 30 monster types and 10 bosses, there is enough opposition to create meaningful challenges, but not enough variety to completely prevent repetition during extended play sessions. The game consequently depends heavily on the player's enjoyment of character advancement and loot acquisition.

A persistent and upgradeable town gives progression another layer beyond the dungeon itself. Developing this hub provides a sense that accomplishments extend beyond individual expeditions. Moving between preparation, character management, town development, exploration, combat, and equipment upgrades creates a dependable gameplay rhythm. It is a straightforward structure, but the interconnected progression systems make it satisfying when the party gradually becomes capable of reaching increasingly difficult sections of the tower.

Presentation is considerably more modest than the underlying character systems. Zavix Tower has the appearance and interface philosophy of an older PC dungeon crawler, which gives it a certain nostalgic personality but can also make it feel dated. Players accustomed to highly polished modern RPGs may find the visuals and interface relatively plain. Storytelling is similarly secondary to mechanics. This is primarily a game about building characters and overcoming increasingly difficult encounters rather than following an elaborate narrative filled with cinematic sequences and heavily developed companions.

Steam Deck compatibility is currently best regarded as unverified rather than officially guaranteed. The game was designed around traditional PC controls and does not carry the same level of confirmed handheld optimization associated with titles that have an official Steam Deck Verified designation. Players interested specifically in portable play should therefore expect that controller configuration, interface readability, or other adjustments may be necessary rather than assuming a completely optimized experience.

Ultimately, Zavix Tower works best for a specific kind of RPG player. Anyone who enjoys turn-based battles, first-person dungeon exploration, extensive character progression, talent experimentation, party composition, randomized equipment, and the pursuit of increasingly powerful builds can find a surprisingly absorbing experience here. Its repetition, restrained presentation, and limited emphasis on narrative prevent it from competing with more ambitious RPGs on spectacle or storytelling, but those qualities matter less when the appeal comes from steadily transforming an ordinary adventuring party into an efficient dungeon-clearing machine.

The game's systems provide enough flexibility to make experimentation rewarding, and its endless structure means dedicated players can continue chasing improvements long after the fundamental mechanics have become familiar. It is not especially flashy, nor does it attempt to reinvent the dungeon-crawler formula, but it understands the satisfaction of incremental advancement and meaningful character optimization. For fans of mechanically focused, old-school fantasy RPGs who value builds and loot more than presentation, Zavix Tower remains a worthwhile niche experience. 

Rating: 6/10
